concepts.definition: A pay-as-you-go deployment that processes requests within the selected Azure geography and does not reserve PTUs.
A pay-as-you-go deployment that can route inference across supported global Azure regions to access more available capacity.
A global deployment that uses reserved provisioned throughput units (PTUs) for predictable capacity.
Reserved model capacity purchased in PTUs to provide predictable throughput for steady workloads.
A language model designed for broad natural-language generation, understanding, and multi-step reasoning.
A smaller language model optimized for lower cost and latency, usually with less capability than a large language model.
A model that converts content into numeric vectors so semantic similarity can be measured.
A model that can process more than one type of input or output, such as text, images, or audio.
Retrieves relevant passages from files made available directly to an agent.
Runs code in an isolated environment for calculations, data analysis, and file processing.
Lets an agent retrieve grounding content from a separately managed Azure AI Search index.
Lets an agent retrieve current public web information and use it as grounding for a response.
A tool that lets an agent interact with a graphical user interface by observing the screen and taking actions.
The model returns a structured function request with arguments; the application executes it and sends back the result.
A tool that lets an agent call HTTP operations described by an OpenAPI specification.
Model Context Protocol, a standard protocol for exposing tools, resources, and prompts to AI clients.
A Foundry workflow provides deterministic steps, conditional branches, shared state, and optional actions without requiring custom orchestration code.
A collaboration pattern in which multiple agents share a conversation and control can pass between them.
An orchestration pattern that passes the output of one step or agent to the next in a fixed order.
An orchestration pattern that pauses execution for human input, review, or approval.
Messages retained within a conversation and used as short-term context for later turns.
Session context preserves state managed by the current orchestration session. It is temporary and not durable cross-conversation memory.
Persistent memory that lets an agent reuse relevant information across separate conversations.
Stores user- or task-specific information that can be retrieved in later conversations.
Retrieves external information at inference time and supplies it as grounding context to a generative model.
Uses a predefined retrieval step to find relevant content before sending the query and retrieved context to the model.
Uses an agent to plan, reformulate, decompose, or repeat retrieval before generating an answer.
Repeats retrieval in multiple passes when the first search does not provide enough useful evidence.
Compares embedding vectors to retrieve semantically similar content even when the wording differs.
Lexical retrieval that matches words and terms in the query against indexed text.
Runs keyword and vector retrieval together and combines their result rankings.
Uses language understanding to rerank an initial search result set for improved relevance.
Defines where indexable content is located and how an Azure AI Search indexer connects to it.
A component that reads content from a data source and populates or refreshes a search index.
A collection of Azure AI Search skills executed as an enrichment pipeline during indexing.
A searchable schema containing fields and documents against which queries run.
Converts text into numeric embedding vectors that can be stored and compared for semantic retrieval.
Splits long text into smaller chunks for indexing, embedding, and retrieval.
Combines text or enriched content into one field inside an Azure AI Search enrichment pipeline.
An Azure AI Search skill that restructures enriched data into a new complex shape.
Microsoft's Azure platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating AI applications and agents.
A managed search service for keyword, vector, hybrid, and semantic retrieval over indexed content.
Analyzes documents, images, audio, or video according to a schema and returns structured, source-grounded fields.
A document AI service for OCR, layout analysis, and structured field extraction.
Azure services for language tasks such as text analysis, entity recognition, and classification.
An Azure service for machine translation of text and documents.
Analyzes visual content to return features such as captions, tags, objects, and detected people.
Collects and visualizes application telemetry such as requests, dependencies, exceptions, performance data, and traces.
Converts printed or handwritten text in images and scanned documents into machine-readable text.
Extracts text, structure, and fields from documents so the content can be processed by an application.
Extracts text together with document structure such as paragraphs, tables, selection marks, and positions.
A prebuilt Document Intelligence model focused on extracting printed and handwritten text.
A cost-effective Content Understanding mode for high-volume analysis of one independent file at a time.
An advanced Content Understanding mode for one file when greater reasoning capability is needed.
An advanced Content Understanding mode that can reason across multiple files and reference data.
Projects binary normalized images from an enrichment tree into Azure Blob Storage.
Projects enriched content as hierarchical JSON objects into Azure Blob Storage.
Projects enriched data as rows and columns into Azure Table Storage.
An Azure-managed identity whose lifecycle is tied to a single Azure resource.
An independent Azure-managed identity that can be attached to one or more Azure resources.
An authentication type that uses the Foundry account's managed identity instead of a stored key.
An authentication pattern that forwards the caller's Microsoft Entra identity to an underlying tool or API.
An Azure Identity credential chain that uses available Microsoft Entra credentials, including managed identity in Azure.
Authenticates an application to Microsoft Entra ID with a tenant ID, client ID, and client secret.
An SDK credential object that authenticates with a static service or API key.
A credential type that authenticates requests by sending a static API key.
A data-plane role that allows an identity to invoke Azure OpenAI model deployments.
A data-plane role that allows an identity to use supported Azure AI services.
A read-oriented data-plane role for service data and metadata.
A broad control-plane role for creating and changing Azure resources, without automatically granting all data-plane permissions.
An Azure data-plane role that allows an identity to read blob data.
An Azure data-plane role that allows an identity to read, write, and delete blob data.
An Azure data-plane role that allows an identity to read and query documents in search indexes.
An Azure data-plane role that allows an identity to add, update, and delete documents in search indexes.
An OpenAPI authentication scheme that defines where an API key must be sent, such as in a request header.
An OpenAPI authentication scheme that sends a bearer token in the Authorization header.
A project connection that provides controlled access to secrets stored in Azure Key Vault.
A connection that uses Microsoft Entra identity and RBAC instead of a stored API key.
Measures whether claims in a response are supported by the supplied source context.
Measures how directly and appropriately a response addresses the user's request or intended task.
Measures grammatical quality, readability, and natural language flow.
Measures whether a response is logically organized and internally consistent.
Measures whether a response covers all information required to answer the task.
Checks whether claims in a generated response are supported by the supplied source context.
Evaluates retrieval and generation quality together in a RAG solution.
Measure harmful, unsafe, or policy-violating content in model inputs or outputs.
Detect direct and indirect prompt-injection attempts that try to override model instructions.
Detect direct prompt-injection attempts in instructions provided by the user.
Detect indirect prompt-injection instructions hidden in retrieved documents or other external content.
Identifies personal information so it can be masked, blocked, or handled according to policy.
Classifies and can block content associated with self-harm according to configured severity thresholds.
Classifies and can block violent content according to configured severity thresholds.
Detects known protected text or code that a model may reproduce.
An application-defined rule that validates or constrains model inputs, outputs, or tool behavior.
Records ordered spans for model calls, tool calls, errors, and timing during an application or agent run.
Measures how many input and output tokens a model request consumes, which helps track usage and cost.
Measures how long a request, model call, tool call, or workflow step takes.
The percentage of agent or workflow runs that complete successfully.
Transcribes streaming speech into text with low latency.
Transcribes prerecorded audio files asynchronously in batch jobs.
Synthesizes spoken audio from written text.
Recognizes spoken input and translates it into another language.
A low-latency realtime media transport commonly used for interactive audio and video in browser or mobile clients.
A persistent bidirectional connection commonly used for server-to-server realtime events and audio streaming.
A signaling protocol used to connect realtime services with telephone and voice communication systems.
Provides a small number of examples in the prompt so the model can imitate the required behavior or format.
Prompts a model to perform a task from instructions without providing demonstration examples.
A parameter that controls how concentrated or varied the model's token probabilities are.
Limits token selection to the smallest candidate set whose cumulative probability reaches p.
A project container for models, deployments, agents, connections, evaluations, and related resources.
A managed service for creating, publishing, and running agents with models, instructions, knowledge, and tools.
An agent whose behavior is defined by a model, instructions, and configured knowledge or tools.
A versioned agent that has been published so applications or workflows can invoke it.
Allows the model to decide whether a tool needs to be used.
Requires the model to make at least one tool call before completing the response.
Prevents the model from using tools for the request.
Forces the model to use the specified tool or tool type.
Persistent storage in which agent memories are saved and searched.
An agent tool that searches for relevant entries in a configured memory store.
A partition key that determines which memories a run can save and retrieve, such as one scope per user.
A documented memory-scope placeholder that partitions persistent agent memory by user identity.
Splits long content into smaller units that can be indexed and retrieved separately.
Repeats some text between neighboring chunks to preserve context across boundaries.
Splits content after a fixed number of tokens or characters regardless of document structure.
Splits content at headings, paragraphs, tables, or other structural boundaries.
A configuration that defines the input modality, schema, and analysis used to produce structured output.
A ready-made analyzer for a common scenario that does not require defining the full field schema.
An analyzer with a user-defined schema for the fields a solution needs to extract or generate.
The definition of field names, data types, descriptions, and generation methods in analyzer output.
A field whose value the model generates or derives from the content according to its schema and instructions.
A field whose value is selected from predefined categories through classification.
An estimate of how certain the analyzer is about an extracted field value.
A reference to the location in the source content that supports an extracted field value.
Allows a deployment to move to a newer default model version under the service's automatic upgrade policy.
Keeps the current model version until it is retired, then upgrades the deployment.

concepts.term: Upgrade when new default is available
concepts.definition: Upgrades the deployment when a new default model version becomes available.
Keeps an explicitly selected model version and requires future version changes to be managed manually.
A subscription- and region-specific limit on how much of a model or service can be deployed or consumed.
A limit on how many requests or tokens can be processed during a time interval.
Increases the waiting time between retries to reduce load and repeated collisions.
Adds random variation to retry delays so many clients do not retry at the same moment.
The proportion of reported positive detections that are correct: TP / (TP + FP).
The proportion of actual positive objects the model finds: TP / (TP + FN).
Mean Average Precision, which summarizes detection precision across classes and often multiple confidence or IoU thresholds.
Intersection over Union, the overlap between predicted and actual bounding boxes divided by their union.
